attachments.text:
ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2020-01-15
Provider: Dr. Sarah Chen, MD
Department: Pulmonology
Visit Type: outpatient

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Progressive difficulty seeing at night and recurrent dry, irritated eyes

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
He also notes increased susceptibility to respiratory and skin infections over the past several months.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Cystic fibrosis with pancreatic insufficiency
- Chronic bronchiectasis
- Chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps

PAST SURGICAL HISTORY:
- Functional endoscopic sinus surgery (2018)
- Tonsillectomy and adenoidectomy (age 8)

MEDICATIONS:
Home Medications:
- Pancrelipase (Creon) 36,000 units lipase with meals and 18,000 units with snacks
- Multivitamin (fat-soluble formulation) 1 tablet daily
- Vitamin D3 (cholecalciferol) 2000 international units daily
- Azithromycin 250 mg orally three times weekly (M/W/F)
- Albuterol HFA inhaler 90 mcg per actuation, 2 inhalations twice daily
- Sodium chloride nasal spray 0.9%, 2 sprays each nostril twice daily

ALLERGIES:
Sulfonamide antibiotics, Iodinated contrast media

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Second cousin diagnosed with cystic fibrosis
- Maternal grandmother with type 2 diabetes mellitus
- Father with hypertension

SOCIAL HISTORY:
His diet consists mostly of rice and bread, with minimal intake of vegetables or animal products.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
Physical examination reveals dry, scaly skin and patches of keratinized conjunctiva on the sclera. The remainder of the examination is unremarkable.

LABORATORY DATA:
Laboratory studies are notable for a low serum concentration of a fat-soluble vitamin.

PATHOLOGY:
Microscopic examination of a skin biopsy shows hyperkeratosis and squamous metaplasia of mucosal surfaces.

attachments.title: Source clinical note
attachments.text:
ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2021-07-15
Provider: Dr. Marcus Rodriguez, MD
Department: Pulmonology
Visit Type: outpatient

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Progressive unintentional weight loss and worsening skin changes

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
The patient is a 38-year-old male with cystic fibrosis and pancreatic insufficiency who presented in January 2020 with difficulty seeing at night and dry, irritated eyes, and now returns with progressive unintentional weight loss and worsening skin changes over the past 3 months. He reports frequent, bulky stools that are difficult to flush and often float in the toilet bowl. He also describes increasing dryness and scaliness of his skin, particularly over the arms and shins, despite using moisturizers. He denies abdominal pain, blood in the stool, or recent travel.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Vitamin A deficiency (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- Cystic fibrosis with pancreatic insufficiency
- Chronic bronchiectasis
- Chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps

PAST SURGICAL HISTORY:
- Functional endoscopic sinus surgery (2018)
- Tonsillectomy and adenoidectomy (age 8)

MEDICATIONS:
Home Medications:
- Pancrelipase (Creon) 36,000 units lipase with meals and 18,000 units with snacks
- Multivitamin (fat-soluble formulation) 1 tablet daily
- Vitamin D3 (cholecalciferol) 2000 international units daily
- Azithromycin 250 mg orally three times weekly (M/W/F)
- Albuterol HFA inhaler 90 mcg per actuation, 2 inhalations twice daily
- Sodium chloride nasal spray 0.9%, 2 sprays each nostril twice daily

ALLERGIES:
Sulfonamide antibiotics, Iodinated contrast media

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Second cousin diagnosed with cystic fibrosis
- Maternal grandmother with type 2 diabetes mellitus
- Father with hypertension

SOCIAL HISTORY:
His diet is unrestricted, and he has no history of alcohol or drug use.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
On exam, he appears thin and has dry, scaly patches on the extensor surfaces of his upper and lower extremities.

LABORATORY DATA:
Laboratory evaluation reveals normocytic anemia. Fecal fat testing is positive.
